descriptionChirho: Prospective perpetuity or unlimited future duration, typically in the prepositional phrase לְעוֹלָם 'to/for eternity' or as a bare/articled noun denoting everlasting continuance; corresponding to Arabic إِلَى الأَبَدِ / لِلأَبَدِ (ila al-abad), Korean 영원히 (yeongwonhi), Swahili milele, Spanish 'para siempre,' Hindi सदा के लिए.

Attributive or adjectival use denoting an enduring, perpetual quality of a noun (covenant, statute, possession, etc.), functioning as a modifier rather than a temporal adverb; corresponding to Arabic أَبَدِيّ / أَبَدِيَّة (abadiyy), Korean 영원한 (yeongwonhan), Swahili ya milele / wa milele, Spanish 'eterno / perpetuo,' Hindi सदा की / अनन्त.

Past-directed eternity or pre-eternity, typically with מִן 'from,' referring to God's eternal existence reaching back without beginning, or to things established from eternity; corresponding to Arabic مِنَ الأَزَلِ / مِنَ الأَبَدِ (min al-azal), Korean 영원에서 / 영원부터 (yeongwon-eseo), Swahili tangu milele / kutoka milele, Spanish 'desde la eternidad,' Hindi अनादिकाल से.

Bounded remote past time or antiquity, not unlimited eternity but historical ancientness, often with מִן 'from' or as a bare noun modifier; corresponding to Arabic الْقِدَمِ / الْقَدِيمِ / قَدِيمًا (al-qidami), Korean 옛날 / 옛 (yennal), Swahili zamani / kale, Spanish 'desde antiguo / antiguo,' Hindi प्राचीन काल / पुराने.

Bounded but extended temporal period(s), generation(s), or era(s), often in the plural עוֹלָמִים; corresponding to Arabic الدُّهُورِ / الأَجْيَالِ (ad-duhur / al-ajyal), Korean 세대들 (sedaedeul), Swahili vizazi / kwa vizazi, Spanish 'siglos / eternidades,' Hindi युगों.
